subject: Clarify pilot billing for transient sessions & aggregation options
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam.park@acmeretail.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procure-acme@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2028-08-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot billing question — short lived sessions + long context

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the retailer-side team is excited to run the 30-day pilot. A quick technical/contracting question came up from procurement and eng: our workload will create many transient inference sessions (user browsing events) that include a fairly large pre-supplied context blob (historical user state ~6k tokens) but each call only generates 10-50 response tokens.

Two questions:
1) How are we billed for the pre-supplied context when it is sent on every short call? Does that count fully per inference request, or is there an aggregation/kv-cache behavior that reduces per-call charges?
2) We’re trying to avoid per-call minimums/rounding causing wild effective price for these bursts. Is there a way to aggregate usage into a short billing window (e.g., 1 minute) or apply a smoothing rule for pilot customers?

Procurement asked for an itemized example (a few rows of math) and an estimate of concessions you can offer for the pilot. I attached our PO (light redactions) for reference.

Appreciate the quick clarification so we can finish paperwork.

—Sam
Senior Product Manager, Acme Retail

Subject: Re: Pilot billing question — short lived sessions + long context

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear outline and for sending the PO. Looping in Karthik (pricing) and Ben (sales ops) to propose concrete math and pilot concessions.

Short answers up-front:
- Context tokens you supply are counted at the time of the request unless we can reuse a cached prefix in the same session or the same KV cache; reuse is possible but depends on how you open/close sessions and whether a pinned context token policy is configured.
- We do have a couple of levers for pilots: temporary smoothing (aggregate short calls into a minute-level window for billing), and temporary waiving/discounting of session minimums for pilot accounts.

I’ll let Karthik lay out a few worked examples and a recommended concession we can include in the pilot SOW.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: Sam Park <sam.park@acmeretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-08-12T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot billing question — short lived sessions + long context

Hi all — following up with concrete examples and an internal recommendation. I also attached a one-tab spreadsheet ("pilot_pricing_tab.xlsx") with the same rows.

Assumptions (for examples below):
- Context blob: 6,000 tokens
- Response size: 30 tokens average per call
- Calls per user per minute: 6 (roughly one every 10s)
- Billing quantum: per-token for input/output, minimum session charge = 50 tokens per request (current default)
- We support temporary "minute aggregation" for pilots if enabled in the console — that aggregates consumption per-user per-minute before applying minimums.

Scenario A: No aggregation (current default)
- Each call billed as max( tokens_used, 50 ) → tokens_used = 6000 + 30 = 6030 -> billed = 6030 tokens per call
- Effective cost per response token is enormous; not realistic for your workload.

Scenario B: KV cache reuse within a session
- If you open a session and keep it alive, the 6k context is stored in KV cache and not re-charged per call; only deltas or position tokens are billed per request.
- Billed per call (after initial warmup): ~30 tokens (response) + small prefix metadata (5–10 tokens) → ~40 billed tokens/call.

Scenario C: Short-lived sessions but with 1-minute aggregation enabled (pilot setting)
- We aggregate all calls originating from the same user identity within 60s and compute total tokens across calls, then apply rounding/minimums once per aggregation window.
- Example math (6 calls/min): total input repeated context = 6 * 6000 = 36,000 input tokens, outputs = 6 * 30 = 180
- If we can identify repeated context and apply a caching heuristic during aggregation, we treat the repeated context as a single billed prefix per minute (this is a heuristical policy for pilots; we log and revert to strict counting post-pilot unless otherwise contracted).
- With caching heuristics: billed tokens ≈ 6,000 (prefix once) + 180 (output) = 6,180 tokens/minute -> after rounding to nearest token, and then apply pilot discount/minimum rules.

Rounding/minimums suggestion for pilot:
- Waive per-call 50-token minimum when 1-minute aggregation is enabled; instead apply a per-minute minimum floor of 200 tokens (covers metadata and warmups) so small spikes aren't penalized.
- Alternatively: apply 50% discount on billed tokens attributable to the prefix (the 6k). This reduces effective cost while we test production characteristics.

Recommended concession for 30-day pilot (proposal):
- Enable 1-minute aggregation for the pilot.
- Waive per-call minimums and apply a per-minute floor of 200 tokens.
- Apply a 40% discount on all tokens attributed to the prefix (context) during pilot.
- Provide a two-week retroactive bill review if observed effective cost deviates >25% from the estimate.

If you prefer a simpler approach for procurement, we can propose a capped pilot budget (e.g., $4,500 total for 30 days) instead of token-level concessions.

Notes and risks:
- Aggregation/caching heuristics are safe for pilot but not guaranteed for long-term billing policy unless encoded in the contract.
- We will surface aggregate metrics in the Console dashboards and tag all pilot usage for traceability.

—Karthik Iyer
Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot billing question — short lived sessions + aggregation options

Vanessa / Karthik — thanks for the worked examples, that helps a lot. Procurement prefers a fixed, itemized line they can sign against rather than relying on later retroactive adjustments. Two asks before we can sign the PO: 

1) Can you produce a single-line pilot price for 30 days that reflects your recommended concession (the aggregation + 40% prefix discount) and a backup capped spend option? We need a dollar value and an internal charge code.
2) Legal/procurement want the smoothing/aggregation behavior written into the SOW for the pilot (not just a console flag). That should include how the prefix identification/heuristic works at a high level and the rollback behavior after the pilot ends.

If you can send a one-page SOW + a single-line invoice amount, we can route the PO and get signatures this week.

—Sam

Sam — great, we can do that. Next steps and what we’ll deliver by end of day Friday: 

1) One-line pilot price: $4,250 for 30 days (covers up to estimated 2M aggregated billed tokens under the pilot assumptions). If you prefer a hard cap we can change to a capped spend line: $4,500 not-to-exceed.
2) One-page SOW: we will include the aggregation behavior, the prefix-identification heuristic summary, and rollback notice (30 days after pilot end unless extended). We will explicitly state that aggregation-and-prefix heuristics are pilot-specific and revert to standard billing absent an executed amendment.
3) Invoice/charge code: HS-987654 (we’ll provide an invoice number once legal approves the SOW).
4) Attachments: pilot_pricing_tab.xlsx (worked examples + per-minute math) and the SOW stub. I’ll also have our contracts lead draft a short amendment for your procurement team.

If this looks good I’ll ask legal/finance to prepare the one-page SOW + invoice and send a DocuSign link. Ben — can you confirm finance is OK with the $4,250 flat pilot and the two-week retroactive review clause? Marissa — please review the SOW language on the rollback/heuristic statement.

Thanks — aiming to get the PO signed and pilot live by Aug 22.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
